title: Borel semidirect product and proper flag quotient over a local ring
statement:
Let $A$ be a nonzero commutative Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and put $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $H$ be a smooth affine finitely presented $S$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, pqf-def-affine-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] whose geometric fibres are connected reductive groups: they have no nontrivial smooth connected normal unipotent subgroup, where unipotent means that all geometric points act by unipotent matrices in a faithful representation. Let $T\subseteq B\subseteq H$ be smooth closed subgroup schemes, with $T\simeq\mathbf G_{m,S}^r$ for some $r\ge0$, such that on every geometric fibre $T$ is a maximal torus and $B$ is a Borel subgroup. Here $\mathbf G_m(C)=C^\times$, a torus over an algebraically closed field is a product of copies of $\mathbf G_m$, maximal means maximal under subgroup inclusion, and a Borel is a maximal smooth connected solvable subgroup; solvable means its iterated derived subgroups become trivial. There is a smooth closed normal subgroup $U\subseteq B$ whose geometric fibres are the unipotent radicals (largest smooth connected normal unipotent subgroups) of those fibres, and multiplication identifies $B$ with $T\ltimes U$. In particular there is a group-scheme projection $p:B\to T$, identity on $T$ with kernel $U$. The fppf sheafification of $C\mapsto H(C)/B(C)$ is represented by a smooth proper $S$-scheme $Q$. Fppf means coverings by flat locally finitely presented morphisms whose images cover. The quotient map $\pi:H\to Q$ is faithfully flat, quasi-compact and locally finitely presented, and
$$H\times_SB\xrightarrow{\sim}H\times_QH,\qquad (g,b)\longmapsto(g,gb).$$
It is thus a right $B$-torsor, meaning precisely this displayed isomorphism and covering property. Formation of $U$, $p$, the quotient and this torsor commutes with arbitrary base change $S'\to S$ [def-pc-base-change]. Under the character identification $X^*(T)\simeq\mathbf Z^r$, let $\Phi\subseteq X^*(T)$ be the set of nonzero weights of $T$ in $\operatorname{Lie}(H)$ (the roots of $H$) and $\Phi^+\subseteq\Phi$ the set of nonzero weights in $\operatorname{Lie}(B)$. Then $\Phi=\Phi^+\sqcup(-\Phi^+)$, and for every geometric fibre $H_{\bar s}$ the restriction isomorphism $X^*(T)\simeq X^*(T_{\bar s})$ carries $\Phi$ onto the nonzero weights of $T_{\bar s}$ in $\operatorname{Lie}(H_{\bar s})$ and $\Phi^+$ onto the nonzero weights of $T_{\bar s}$ in $\operatorname{Lie}(B_{\bar s})$. A weight means a character eigensummand for the full adjoint torus coaction, not just the action on $A$-points; $\operatorname{Lie}(B)$ is its tangent module at the identity, defined by dual numbers. When $H=T$ the conclusions include $U=1$ and $Q=S$.

source.place: Conrad, Reductive group schemes, Definition 5.1.1 and discussion (printed p.136); Proposition 5.2.3 (p.152), Corollary 5.2.5 (pp.153--154), Corollary 5.2.8 (pp.155--156), Theorem 5.2.11 and proof of Corollary 5.2.13 (pp.157--159). Local PDF WANTED as literature/conrad-reductive-group-schemes.pdf; primary author PDF read online.

proof.text: First check finiteness for all applications below. Write $H=\operatorname{Spec}C$. Its finite presentation over $A$ makes $C$ finite type, hence Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]. Since $B$ and $T$ are closed in $H$, their coordinate algebras are quotients of $C$, hence finite type over $A$ and Noetherian. Their ideals in $C$ are finitely generated by the definition of Noetherianity, so the closed inclusions are finitely presented. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-noetherian-finite-presentation], $B$ and $T$ are finitely presented over $A$. More generally an $A$-map between affine finite-type $A$-schemes is finitely presented: its source algebra is generated over the target algebra by its finitely many $A$-algebra generators, and the target algebra is Noetherian by the first cited lemma, so the second applies. This also handles every map between the affine dynamic subgroups below.

source.place: Finiteness bookkeeping for Proposition 5.2.3, pp.152--153; Stacks algebra.tex Tags 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence) and 00FP (lemma-Noetherian-finite-type-is-finite-presentation).

proof.text: Put $M=\mathbf Z^r$, $\mathfrak h=\operatorname{Lie}(H)$ and $\mathfrak b=\operatorname{Lie}(B)$. Apply [lem-sfb-relative-tangent-weight-base-change] to conjugation by $T$ on $H$ and on $B$. These modules have finitely many weight summands, each finite projective, and all weight summands commute with every scalar extension. The inclusions of tangent modules are weight preserving, since the group inclusions commute with conjugation. Each finite projective summand is free over $A$: apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-projective-prime-local-free] at the maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$; the resulting $f\notin\mathfrak m$ is a unit, so its standard neighbourhood is the whole spectrum. A free summand is nonzero exactly when its scalar extension to an algebraic closure $F$ of $A/\mathfrak m$ is nonzero. Consequently the nonzero weight sets $\Phi$ and $\Phi^+$ for $H$ and $B$ respectively are the same on every geometric fibre. A closed subgroup has injective tangent map on each fibre: on dual-number points its kernel is the identity. In particular $\Phi^+\subseteq\Phi$.

source.place: Section 4, opening, p.107 (graded tangent bundle); Proposition 5.2.3, proof, p.152 (weight subbundles).

proof.text: The character labels used in step 2 are the actual characters of $T$ and of every geometric fibre. Indeed [lem-sfb-relative-diagonalizable-character-duality], with target $\mathbf G_m$, says that such characters are locally Laurent monomials. A locally constant label on the spectrum of a local ring is constant: an open neighbourhood of its closed point contains a standard open $D(f)$ with $f\notin\mathfrak m$, hence is the whole spectrum. Thus restriction identifies both character groups with $M$. On the closed geometric fibre apply [lem-sfb-borel-opposite-root-dichotomy] to $(H_F,T_F,B_F)$. Together with step 2 it gives $\Phi=\Phi^+\sqcup(-\Phi^+)$. The same weight-base-change statement proves the required restriction assertions at every other geometric point, with characters rather than their differentials, including in positive characteristic.

source.place: Definition 5.1.1, p.136; Proposition 5.2.3, proof, p.152; Appendix B.1, pp.280--281.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-regular-cocharacter-borel-description] on the closed geometric fibre: choose a regular $\lambda_F:\mathbf G_{m,F}\to T_F$ with $B_F=P_{H_F}(\lambda_F)$. It is an integer tuple under $T_F\simeq\mathbf G_{m,F}^r$ by [lem-sfb-relative-diagonalizable-character-duality]. Use the same tuple of monomials to define $\lambda:\mathbf G_{m,A}\to T$. Its pairings are positive on $\Phi^+$ and negative on $-\Phi^+$, because the tangent formula in the first cited node has exactly these nonzero weights on the closed fibre. The zero-weight map $\operatorname{Lie}(T)\to\mathfrak h_0$ is an isomorphism on the closed fibre: [lem-sfb-reductive-cocharacter-parabolic-geometry] gives $Z_{\lambda_F}=T_F$, and [lem-sfb-relative-dynamic-subgroups] identifies its tangent with the zero-weight part. Likewise $\mathfrak b_0=\mathfrak h_0$ and $\mathfrak b_\alpha=\mathfrak h_\alpha$ for $\alpha\in\Phi^+$ on that fibre, by the same dynamic tangent formula for $B_F$. These are isomorphisms over $A$: their source and target are finite free by step 2, of equal rank, and a square matrix invertible modulo $\mathfrak m$ has determinant outside $\mathfrak m$, hence a unit. All other nonzero summands of $\mathfrak b$ vanish. Therefore $\mathfrak b=\operatorname{Lie}(T)\oplus\bigoplus_{\alpha\in\Phi^+}\mathfrak h_\alpha$ as submodules of $\mathfrak h$.

source.place: Proposition 5.2.3, proof, pp.152--153: lift the closed-fibre cocharacter and compare tangent weight spaces.

proof.text: For conjugation by $\lambda$, form $P_H,U_H,Z_H$ and $P_B$ using [lem-sfb-relative-dynamic-subgroups]. Their formation commutes with every base change; they are smooth affine finitely presented closed groups. The group $B$ has geometrically connected fibres by the Borel hypothesis, so $P_B$ does too. Its tangent inclusion into $\mathfrak b$ is an equality: step 4 says that every $\lambda$-weight of $\mathfrak b$ is nonnegative, and the cited dynamic tangent formula selects exactly those weights. On every geometric fibre apply [lem-sfb-smooth-subgroup-tangent-generation] to the smooth connected group $B_{\bar s}$, the single smooth connected subgroup $(P_B)_{\bar s}$, and $K=(P_B)_{\bar s}$ itself. The tangent spanning condition holds, hence $(P_B)_{\bar s}=B_{\bar s}$. The isomorphism clause of [lem-sfb-flat-geometric-fibre-open-criterion] now gives $P_B=B$ over $A$; the source is smooth and the maps are finitely presented by step 1. This does not infer equality of unrelated closed subschemes merely from their fibres.

source.place: Proposition 5.2.3, proof, pp.152--153: $P_Q(\lambda)=Q$ and comparison with $P_G(\lambda)$.

proof.text: An orbit extension inside $B$ is also an orbit extension inside $H$, so $P_B=B$ factors through $P_H$ as a closed subgroup. This can be checked on coordinate ideals: the negative-degree generators cutting out $P_H$ map to zero in $A[P_B]$. The tangent formula of [lem-sfb-relative-dynamic-subgroups] and step 4 give $\operatorname{Lie}(P_H)=\mathfrak b$. On each geometric fibre both groups are smooth and connected. Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-subgroup-tangent-generation] with ambient $(P_H)_{\bar s}$ and subgroup $B_{\bar s}$ to conclude equality, then apply [lem-sfb-flat-geometric-fibre-open-criterion] as in step 5 to get $B=P_H$. The constant orbit gives an inclusion $T\to Z_H$. On every geometric fibre regularity and [lem-sfb-reductive-cocharacter-parabolic-geometry] give $T_{\bar s}=(Z_H)_{\bar s}$. Apply the same fibre isomorphism criterion to this map between smooth groups to obtain $T=Z_H$. Put $U=U_H$ and $p=q$. The dynamic theorem gives the smooth closed normal $U$, the multiplication isomorphism $T\ltimes U\simeq B$, the retraction $p$ and $\ker p=U$.

source.place: Proposition 5.2.3 and Corollary 5.2.5, pp.152--154; Theorem 4.1.7, pp.112--114.

proof.text: For a geometric point, write $R=R_u(B_{\bar s})$ for the radical supplied by [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure]. The dynamic subgroup $U_{\bar s}$ is smooth connected normal unipotent by [lem-sfb-relative-dynamic-subgroups], so maximality of $R$ gives $U_{\bar s}\subseteq R$. Conversely $p_{\bar s}|_R:R\to T_{\bar s}$ is trivial by [lem-sfb-unipotent-to-multiplicative-trivial], since $R$ is unipotent and $T_{\bar s}$ is a torus. Hence $R\subseteq\ker(p_{\bar s})=U_{\bar s}$. This proves precisely the claimed radical identification on every geometric fibre, without a reduced-base assumption.

source.place: Corollary 5.2.5, pp.153--154 (identifying the dynamic kernel with the fibrewise radical).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-relative-smooth-subgroup-normalizer] to $B\subseteq H$. Its closed finite-presentation hypothesis was checked in step 1; smoothness is assumed, and geometric connectedness follows from being a Borel on each geometric fibre. It yields a finitely presented closed normalizer $N$ and $B\hookrightarrow N$, compatible with arbitrary base change. On every geometric fibre [lem-sfb-borel-scheme-normalizer] identifies $N_{\bar s}$ with $B_{\bar s}$ on all test algebras, not only field points. Use [lem-sfb-flat-geometric-fibre-open-criterion] to conclude $B=N$. Here the source $B/S$ is smooth, hence flat and locally finitely presented by [lem-pc-smooth-flat]; $N/S$ is finite type; and $B\to N$ is finitely presented by step 1 (alternatively its ideal is the image of the finitely generated ideal defining $B$ in $H$). The criterion does not require $N$ to be flat.

For every geometric fibre, $B_{\bar s}=P_{H_{\bar s}}(\lambda_{\bar s})$ by step 6 and dynamic base change. The field theorem [lem-sfb-reductive-cocharacter-parabolic-geometry] therefore gives a smooth projective scheme representing $H_{\bar s}/B_{\bar s}$. Now [lem-sfb-relative-self-normalizing-quotient] applies to $B\subseteq H$: both are smooth affine finitely presented, both have geometrically connected nonempty fibres, $B$ is a finitely presented closed subgroup by step 1, and self-normalization was proved in step 8. Its properness hypothesis is exactly the geometric projectivity just verified. Thus the fppf coset sheaf is represented by a smooth proper $S$-scheme $Q$, and $\pi:H\to Q$ is a smooth surjective right $B$-torsor with the displayed kernel-pair isomorphism. Smoothness gives flatness and local finite presentation by [lem-pc-smooth-flat], so $\pi$ is faithfully flat and locally finitely presented.

It remains to check quasi-compactness of $\pi$. The affine scheme $H$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], since $H/S$ is finitely presented and $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ is Noetherian. For an affine open $V\subseteq Q$, $W=\pi^{-1}(V)$ is open in $H$. Its inclusion is quasi-compact by [lem-sfb-noetherian-open-immersion-qc]. Since $H$ itself is affine, the definition of quasi-compactness of that inclusion says exactly that $W$ is quasi-compact. This is the required quasi-compactness of $\pi$.

source.place: Finiteness supplement to Corollary 5.2.8; Stacks morphisms.tex Tag 01T6 (lemma-finite-type-noetherian), and properties.tex Tag 01OX (lemma-immersion-into-noetherian).

proof.text: For arbitrary $S'\to S$, pull back the chosen cocharacter and group diagrams. The arbitrary-base-change clause of [lem-sfb-relative-dynamic-subgroups] identifies $U_{S'}$ with the same contraction subgroup, and identifies $p_{S'}$ with evaluation at zero. Since $B=P_H$ and $T=Z_H$ as group schemes, their pullbacks have these same identifications. Thus the semidirect multiplication, kernel and retraction are literally the pulled-back maps, and the geometric radicals are those proved in step 7. The arbitrary-base-change clause of [lem-sfb-relative-self-normalizing-quotient] identifies $Q_{S'}$ and its torsor with the sheaf quotient $H_{S'}/B_{S'}$ and its kernel pair. The torsor isomorphism is still $(g,b)\mapsto(g,gb)$ because it uses the pulled-back group multiplication. These identifications also respect successive base changes, by the same functorial formulas. Non-affine $S'$ cause no issue: the dynamic identifications agree on affine overlaps, as the orbit-extension condition is intrinsic.

source.place: Theorem 4.1.7, pp.112--114 and the base-change discussion p.114; Corollary 5.2.8 and Theorem 2.3.6.

proof.text: If $H=T$, the inclusions $T\subseteq B\subseteq H$ force $B=H$. There are no nonzero adjoint weights, so choose $\lambda=0$. Its conjugation action is trivial, hence its contraction kernel is the identity group and $p$ is the identity. Every coset is the unique coset; thus the quotient sheaf is the terminal $S$-sheaf represented by $S$, and the torsor map is $H\to S$. This includes $r=0$. No assumption that $A$ is reduced, a field, henselian, or of fixed residue characteristic has been introduced.

source.place: Empty-root case in Definition 5.1.1 and Theorem 4.1.7; direct verification from the definitions.
